page.description: SystemRescue editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A bootable Linux repair toolkit based on Arch Linux (archiso) with XFCE desktop and systemd, providing disk and filesystem administration tools for system recovery.
pros: Complete toolkit: GParted, fsarchiver, ddrescue, testdisk, ntfs-3g, memtest86+.
XFCE GUI plus six virtual consoles — graphical or full command-line.
Boots on both legacy BIOS and UEFI without repartitioning.
SHA-256, SHA-512 and detached GPG signature published per release.
cons: x86_64 only — i386 dropped since v9.04.
No published EOL or support window; only the newest release is current.
Secure Boot support not documented by the publisher.
ZFS not included due to licensing ambiguity.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for SystemRescue; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick with dd or Rufus in ISO mode; writing erases the stick. Boot from the USB and use the live environment — no installation to disk is required for normal operation.

editions.name: Live Rescue ISO
editions.description: The single live rescue ISO for x86_64/amd64 — boots to XFCE desktop with startx, plus six virtual consoles for command-line administration.
editions.usbNote: 1.3 GB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.
